ar_slapstick_wall.blurb: Slapstick Wall is a small sport wall in the Lake Lincoln area of northwest Arkansas, roughly 30 to 40 minutes west of Fayetteville. The stone here is good quality and runs from vertical to overhanging. All five routes sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers who already lead that grade and want a short, steep tick list rather than a big day out. The wall lies north of the boulder cluster and is reached on a climbers' trail that starts from either the Mad Max or Ivory Coast areas. Top-roping has been done here, and a few older cold shuts remain high up.

ar_lone_wadi_point.blurb: Lone Wadi Point is a small sport crag within the Lone Wadi climbing area near Hopewell, Arkansas. It holds five bolted routes, spread from about 5.9 up through the 5.11 range with the bulk of them at 5.11, so it favors climbers comfortable on harder sport leads. The wider Lone Wadi area is known for surprisingly tall bolted lines and a number of boulder problems, and rock quality there swings from soft and sandy in some spots to very hard around the next corner. Expect a short visit here rather than a full day of mileage.

ar_coyote_cave.blurb: Coyote Cave is a small bouldering spot on the north end of Fitzgerald Mountain in northwest Arkansas, tucked into a cavey ridgeline of columns, cracks and roofs. The five problems run from V1 to V3, most of them at the easy end. Holds are scarce, so you need to be creative to find anything fun. The main cave is the second one along the trail and is the biggest, with several openings you can walk straight into. The trail carries mountain bikers at speed, so take care when arriving, leaving or topping out onto it.
ar_coyote_cave.approach: From the main trail fork, follow the signs for Coyote Cave. The main cave is the second one you reach, and you can step directly into it from the trail.

ar_roof_the.blurb: The Roof is a bouldering cave in the Never Never Land section of Jamestown Crag, a short drive from Batesville in northeast Arkansas. It is an overhanging roof of good quality stone, and the five problems run from V3 up to the V6 to V7 range. The climbing is steep and powerful, so come ready for kneebars, toe hooks and inverted moves. The low end of the cave tends to seep and stay wet, though most problems begin above the damp zone. It sits between the 5.8 routes and the Magic Carpet Ride line.

ar_down_under_wall.blurb: Down Under Wall is a short cliff in The Outback, part of the Sam's Throne area of north-central Arkansas. It offers a mix of face and crack climbing with both sport and trad lines on good rock. Its five routes span roughly 5.9 to 5.12, with most at 5.10 and above, so it is better for climbers with some experience than for beginners. It sits between Outback Wall and Seed Wall along the line of walls running out from the Dog Walkdown, and it begins at a large black dihedral with a permanent pool beneath it.
